content:
alex: hey folks — quick request: I opened a small change that touches runtime batching defaults and adds a tiny security header check. need runtime + platform + security eyes so we can merge during the next dev-hour. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/824 (short diff)

maya: thanks alex — pinged platform owners. do we need a canary or is this safe to ship to prod?

alex: leaning safe for prod but would prefer a short canary (30m) for the traffic pattern change. it's basically lowering batch_window_ms from 12 -> 8 and adding a header validation on incoming websocket handshakes.

leo: runtime note: lowering batch window could increase RPC frequency under low qps. did you evaluate tail-latency on 1k qps tests?

alex: ran a quick local sim — p50/p95 looked fine, tail had a handful of outliers. attaching the snippet I used:
```bash
python tools/load_gen.py --clients 50 --qps 1000 --seq-dist short
# results: p50 32ms, p95 120ms, p99 420ms
```

leo: ok can you add a metric tag so we can filter canary by batch_window? otherwise we'll lose attribution.

nina: security: quick read — header validation looks good but need to confirm we don't start accepting unvalidated cookie payloads. also add a short threat-model note in the PR description: what this header prevents and any failure modes. will also check KMS usage if keys are touched.

alex: good call — will add the threat-model blurb and the metric tag.

sam: infra: if this changes connection churn we should throttle control-plane ops. suggest we schedule the canary right after the hourly autoscaler window. cc @maya for timing.

maya: we have a 10:30–11:00 dev-hour slot free. if runtime + security sign off by 10:20 I can kick the canary then.

ops-bot: CI status — runtime/pull/824: build ✅, unit tests ✅, integration tests flaky (1 test failed, rerun recommended).

alex: thanks bot. i'll rerun the flaky test and push the threat-model and metric tag by 10:00.

leo: once those are in i can give a quick approve for runtime side. nina, maya — any blockers from security/platform?

nina: no blockers after the blurb and KMS confirm. i'll review once updated.

maya: platform ok with canary plan, will coordinate the window and watch dashboards.

alex: perfect — plan: push updates by 10:00, request final thumbs up, canary 10:30–11:00, rollback plan: revert batch_window to 12 and scale down canary.

leo: 👍 will keep an eye on kv-cache hit-rate and per-token latency.

nina: 👍

maya: :thumbsup:

alex: thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turn.
